questions.q: What did the 2017 study comparing judges with a computer program find?
a: Defendants the judges released were 25% more likely to reoffend
The computer released far more defendants overall
Judges and the program agreed in nearly every case
The program proved worse at predicting reoffending
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the people judges granted bail reoffended more often than the program's choices would have.

questions.q: What does Gladwell call our default when judging other people?
a: We assume people are telling the truth
We assume people are hiding something
We look for signs of nervousness
We compare them with ourselves
questions.why: Lesson 2 says we believe people by default and only shift when we get clear evidence of a lie.

questions.q: How accurate were people at spotting liars in Tim Levine's experiments?
a: About 54% of the time
About 80% of the time
About 30% of the time
About 95% of the time
questions.why: Lesson 2 says accuracy hovered barely above a coin flip across repeated runs.

questions.q: How many participants showed the typical wide-eyed, jaw-dropped look of surprise?
a: Only about five percent
About half of them
Nearly all of them
About one in four
questions.why: Lesson 3 says almost nobody matched the standard facial expression we expect for surprise.

questions.q: Why did police suspect Amanda Knox after her roommate's murder?
a: Her behavior did not look like the grief they expected
She had been seen near the crime scene that night
Her fingerprints were found on the weapon
She had argued with Kercher earlier that day
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Knox showed affection to her boyfriend instead of mourning, which police read as guilt.
